     Edit the document in that repository, not this file. -->

Sourcing looks for things you could buy in a shop and sell on Amazon at a
profit. It reads the shelves of the retailers you choose, finds every
product with a barcode, looks each one up on Amazon, and keeps the ones
that would still make money after Amazon has taken its real cut.

It never buys anything. It finds a deal and shows you the evidence; buying
is yours.

The Sourcing page shows these four figures while a scan runs, so you can
watch it work:

1. **Pages read.** Biryar opens the shop's public pages, a few seconds
   apart, the way a careful visitor would.
2. **Products with a barcode.** A product can be matched to Amazon only
   through its barcode (the EAN, or the ISBN on a book). A page can list
   several products.
3. **Looked up on Amazon.** Each barcode is looked up once, through Keepa,
   which says what the product sells for on Amazon and how often it sells.
4. **Deals.** A product is kept only if money is left after the shelf
   price and after the fees Amazon really takes, measured from your own
   sales. See [How the fees are measured](/methodology/fees/).

## What you need first

- **A Keepa key**, for every scan. See [Keepa](/setup/keepa/).
- **A ScraperAPI key**, only for some shops. In the list of retailers each
  shop says one of two things: **no key needed**, or **needs ScraperAPI**.
  See [ScraperAPI](/setup/scraperapi/).

Both go under **Settings, Connections**.

## Starting a scan yourself

On the **Sourcing** page, under **New scan**:

1. Tick the retailers to read.
2. Choose how many pages to read in all. Two hundred is a good first
   scan. If you tick several shops, the pages are shared between them, and
   you can give one shop a larger share.
3. Press **Start the scan**.

Each retailer then has its own line: how many pages it read, how many
products and deals it found, and, when it stops, why. **Stop it** ends a
scan early; everything read and priced up to then is kept.

A scan does not have to read a whole shop in one go. The next scan of the
same shop carries on from where the last one stopped.

## Shops that keep running by themselves

On Pro, a shop can be scanned by itself, day after day, without anyone
pressing Start. This is set under **Settings, Sourcing**, in the card
called **Kept running**:

1. Switch the retailer on.
2. Choose how many passes a day it gets, from 1 to 48.
3. Press **Save changes**. Nothing changes until you do.

The rules, in plain words:

- **You do not press Start for these.** A retailer switched on here is
  scanned by itself for as long as the computer is on.
- **Passes are spread evenly over the day.** One pass a day is once a day;
  four is every six hours; 24 is every hour. The first one starts within a
  minute or two of saving.
- **Each pass reads up to 200 pages and carries on where the last
  stopped**, so a shop is read from its first page to its last over time,
  and then starts again. The column called Laps counts how many times it
  has been read through.
- **Scans you start yourself are separate.** They do not count towards the
  number of passes, and they do not delay them.
- **Two at a time.** If several shops are due at the same moment, two run
  and the rest wait their turn. The page says "Queued" for the ones
  waiting.
- **A pass your scraping account refuses is tried again.** If ScraperAPI
  refuses before a single page is read, most often because its credits are
  used up, the pass does not count. Biryar tries again once an hour and
  carries on by itself when the account answers.

The Sourcing page shows these shops first, in a card called **Running by
itself**: which one is running now, when each last ran and what it found,
and when the next pass is due.

### What a schedule costs

Every product looked up on Amazon spends one Keepa token, and a Keepa plan
refills a fixed number of tokens a minute. So a schedule can ask for more
than your plan gives.

Under the list of retailers, **What this schedule costs** adds it up for
you: how many tokens a day your schedule spends, how many your Keepa plan
refills, and what share that is. It updates while you change the numbers,
before you save. If the schedule is too large for the plan, it says so and
suggests a number of passes a day that fits.

Running out of tokens is harmless. The pass stops, says so, and the next
one carries on from the same place once the tokens have refilled.

## Reading the deals

**Deals found** lists everything that would make money, best first.

| Column | What it means |
|---|---|
| Shelf | The price in the shop today. |
| Amazon | The price it sells for on Amazon today. |
| Profit / unit | What is left from one sale after the shelf price and Amazon's real cut. |
| ROI | That profit as a share of what you paid. 40% means every €10 spent brings €4 back on top. |
| Sells / day | How many are sold on Amazon in a day, counted from Keepa's record of the last one to three months. It is a cautious figure: the real number is at least this. A dash means Keepa did not say. |

Each row has three links:

- **Shop** opens the product in the retailer's shop.
- **Amazon** opens its Amazon listing.
- **Keepa** opens its Keepa page, with the history of its price and sales
  rank, for a closer look before you buy.

Click a row to see the evidence behind the figures: the fees Amazon would
take, the cost including what you cannot reclaim, the sales rank and the
barcode. **Download** saves the whole list as a file a spreadsheet can
open, links included.

Above the list you can switch between **This scan** and **All scans**, and
show one retailer on its own.

A deal is a fact about today's prices, not a promise. Before buying, look
at the Keepa page: a price that has only just risen on Amazon may fall
back.

## Why a scan stopped

Every retailer's line says why it stopped. These are the reasons you will
see, and what to do about each.

| It says | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| It read the pages it was given | Nothing went wrong. | Nothing. The next scan carries on. |
| Your ScraperAPI credits are used up | The scraping account refused. Nothing is wrong with the shop. | Top up ScraperAPI, or wait for its monthly refill. Scheduled passes carry on by themselves. |
| The scraping account's plan does not include an option this retailer needs | A few shops need a larger ScraperAPI plan. | Waiting will not help. Use a larger plan, or leave that shop out. |
| The scraping service rejected the key | The ScraperAPI key is wrong or was cancelled. | Paste the key again under Settings, Connections. |
| This retailer needs a scraping key and none is set | The shop says "needs ScraperAPI" and there is no key. | Add a ScraperAPI key. |
| The Keepa token balance ran out | Keepa's tokens are spent for now. | Nothing. They refill, and the scan picks up where it stopped. |
| Keepa rejected the key | The Keepa key is wrong or the subscription ended. | Check it under Settings, Connections. |
| The shop refused to answer Biryar | The shop does not answer programs. | See [ScraperAPI](/setup/scraperapi/). |
| The worker stopped partway | The computer slept or was restarted. | Nothing. What was read is kept. |
| You stopped it | You pressed Stop it. | Nothing. What was read and priced is kept. |

## A scan found nothing

That is a real answer, and usually one of these:

- The shop's prices are not below Amazon's once the real fees are taken
  off. Most shops, most days.
- Keepa does not carry what the shop sells.
- The scan read only a small part of a large shop. Later scans read the
  rest.
- A key ran out of tokens or credits. The retailer's line says so.

## Free and Pro

On the free plan you can start two scans a day, of up to three retailers
each, and each scan shows its best hundred results. Every retailer is
available on both plans. Pro removes those limits, keeps retailers running
by themselves, and lets you add a retailer of your own. See
[Free and Pro](/plans/).

## How Biryar behaves in a shop

It says who it is, reads the shop's own rules for programs first and
follows them, waits at least three seconds between two pages, and does
not ask for the same page twice in a day. It reads public product pages
only: never a basket, an account or a checkout. Shop owners can read more
at <https://biryar.ciyalabs.com/bot/>.
